forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

summary.summary: This is the covering report introducing the Chief Finance Officer's Treasury Management 2025/26 Annual Report, which itself will go to full Council on 16 July 2026 as Annex 1; that annex (with the outturn figures, borrowing, investment maturity and prudential-indicator tables) was not included in the packet supplied to this reading, so no borrowing, CFR or investment figures could be grounded from what was read. What the covering report does confirm is two proposed amendments to the 2026/27 Treasury Management Strategy: excluding Hart and Rushmoor councils from individual counterparty limits for local-authority loans, and raising the Prudential Limit for 'Long-Term Principal Investments to Mature' in 2027/28 and 2028/29. Both changes loosen existing limits rather than tighten them, which is worth a lender's attention even though the covering report gives no revised limit figures.

signals.headline: Council proposes raising the Prudential Limit for 'Long-Term Principal Investments to Mature' in 2027/28 and 2028/29, and excluding Hart and Rushmoor from individual counterparty limits, rather than tightening either
signals.why: Raising a prudential limit and loosening a counterparty concentration limit both increase the amount of exposure the council permits itself, rather than reducing risk.

news_drafts.headline: Basingstoke and Deane draft budget balances 2027/28 and 2028/29, with a £1.57m gap in 2029/30
news_drafts.lead:
Basingstoke and Deane Borough Council's draft medium term financial strategy (MTFS) shows a balanced budget for 2027/28 and 2028/29, according to the budget report before Cabinet on 10 November 2026. For 2029/30 it shows a gap of £1.57m.

The report sets out the position after Cabinet's proposals. The 2029/30 figure is lower than the £1.93m gap in the MTFS update presented to Council in February 2026. In the report's words: "This is a reduction from the £1.93M budget gap contained in the MTFS update presented to Council in February 2026."

The report states that the 2029/30 gap will need to be addressed for the council to set a balanced budget in that year.

news_drafts.headline: Basingstoke and Deane's auditor expects a qualified opinion, with its scope still to be decided
news_drafts.lead:
Basingstoke and Deane Borough Council's external auditor, which carries out the independent check on its accounts, expects to give a qualified audit opinion, meaning it could not fully sign off the accounts. It has not yet decided which areas the qualification will cover. The position is set out in an appendix to the Audit and Accounts Committee papers for its meeting on 28 September.

The auditor is still rebuilding its assurance over the council's reserves, the money it has put aside, after earlier years in which it gave no opinion at all. Four balances are marked "to be confirmed" rather than as fully or partly assured: the General Fund Balance, the Revaluation Reserve, the Capital Adjustment Account and the Pooled Investments Fund.

The paper says: "Although a qualification is anticipated, the basis and scope of that qualification will be determined upon completion of the remaining audit procedures." The rebuilding work was commissioned under the audit recovery programme of the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government.

findings.headline: Council has an obligation to provide 250 car parking spaces for the AA at Basing View, which must be relocated after Fanum House demolition
findings.detail: The paper says a decision has been taken to demolish Fanum House to ready the plot for future development and reduce holding costs, including business rates and security. As a result, the parking for the AA will need to be relocated, with a revenue pressure from reduced car park income.
findings.matters: A demolition decision on a commercial site creates a revenue consequence through a contractual parking obligation, which other councils with redevelopment plans may face.
findings.figures: 250 spaces to be provided; pressure of £0.05M a year from 2027/28 (table)
findings.quote: The council has an obligation to provide 250 car parking spaces for the AA at Basing View.

findings.headline: Car parking income budget to rise by £60,000 a year, with £40,000 anticipated in 2027/28 because of The Malls resurfacing
findings.detail: Parking revenues have continued to exceed forecast over the last two financial years. The paper says resurfacing works at The Malls car park, not expected to finish until June 2027, may temporarily reduce capacity, so the full £60,000 is expected only from 2028/29.
findings.matters: It shows a capital works programme affecting income in the year it is delivered, and the timing shift that follows.
findings.quote: it is anticipated that only £40,000 of additional income will be achievable during 2027/28

findings.headline: Cemetery plot sales income at Worting Road expected to decline over the medium term
findings.detail: Worting Road Cemetery is approaching capacity for standard interments and heritage plots cannot be bought in advance and earn less. The paper says residents can now buy standard plots at North Waltham Cemetery, which is expected to reduce demand for the higher-value plots.
findings.matters: It shows a fee-income stream falling as a site reaches capacity, which is relevant to any council with a cemetery nearing full capacity.
findings.figures: £0.04M a year income reduction in 2027/28, 2028/29 and 2029/30 (table)
findings.quote: Income from cemetery plot sales is expected to continue to decline over the medium term

findings.headline: Management fee for the new leisure contract with Places Leisure from 1 January 2027 adds £0.60M in 2027/28, falling to £0.20M by 2029/30
findings.detail: The new leisure contract will require management fee payments to the operator in its first few years, until the new Leisure Park water and leisure facility is built. The budget covers the Aquadrome, Tadley Swimming Pool and the Golf Centre, and is offset by no longer paying Serco, the outgoing contractor.
findings.matters: A council paying a contractor a management fee while a capital facility is built is a pattern other councils with leisure PFI or capital-linked contracts may recognise.
findings.figures: £0.60M in 2027/28, £0.37M in 2028/29, £0.20M in 2029/30 (table); offset by savings from not paying Serco (not quantified in paper)
findings.quote: will require payments to the operator in the first few years until the new Leisure Park water and leisure facility is built.

findings.headline: £100,000 a year AI and digital invest-to-save saving removed from the MTFS, with the paper citing uncertainty from local government reorganisation
findings.detail: The 2026/27 MTFS included a net invest-to-save saving of £100,000 a year from accelerating AI and digital work. The paper proposes removing it, partly offset by reducing the digital budget that would have supported the work, and records 2.0 FTE removed.
findings.matters: It is a savings line that has been dropped, and the reason given is the future LGR position, which other councils facing reorganisation will also have to consider.
findings.figures: £100,000 a year saving removed; pressure of £0.10M a year from 2027/28 (table); -2.0 FTE
findings.quote: The ability to deliver this major change and introduce the savings is uncertain given the future LGR position, therefore at this stage it is proposed that the saving is removed from the MTFS.

daily_post.headline: Q1 forecast shows £0.02M overspend against budgeted surplus, signalling emerging pressures to be addressed in Medium Term Financial Strategy update.
daily_post.lead: Demonstrates emerging pressures from housing subsidy, service inflation, and cost base growth, though council remains in surplus.
